subject: Interim mitigation plan for service suppression + customer-facing readout
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jackie Zhou <jackie@bluecart.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Interim mitigation plan for service suppression + customer-facing readout

Morning team —

BlueCart reported an uptick in end-user 95/99 latency and concurrent request throttling starting ~08:40 UTC; they observed a ~3–4x p95 and a 20% drop in sustained throughput for their gen endpoints. Jackie is copied so we can keep the external timeline in sync.

Quick summary of what we know so far: 
- Impact window: ~08:40 — ongoing (first ping to us at 08:51).
- Symptoms: p95 tail increases, some 504/Retry responses for long-streaming jobs, overall qps down ~20%.
- Preliminary telemetry: rapid KV cache miss rate spike and increased GPU warm-up churn on the pools servicing BlueCart routes. I attached a snapshot of the KV eviction events we pulled at 09:00.

Primary asks (internal):
1) Ben / Marcus: confirm whether autoscaler stepdown (rolling control-plane upgrade) at 08:30 could have caused transient node recycling resulting in widespread KV cache evaporation. If so, what mitigations do we have short-term (pin pools, increase warmstart buffer, accelerate cache repopulation)?
2) Soojin / Marissa: prepare a 1-paragraph proactive note for BlueCart that explains: what happened at a high level, immediate mitigation steps, and our timeline for a root cause update. Keep it concise and non-technical. Jackie — we’ll send a draft to you first.
3) Product ask: if this is an orchestrator/control-plane induced cache churn, we need a near-term guardrail (rollback of that rollout to avoid evictions) + a design ticket to add cache-safe rollout semantics. Marcus, can you scope the design/ETA?

Suggested immediate mitigation (we can action after engineer confirmation):
- Pause the in-flight control-plane rollout for the affected pools.
- Temporarily route BlueCart traffic to warm standby pools with pinned model variants to reduce cold starts.
- Enable a short-lived higher KV cache retention policy for BlueCart tenant (5–10 minutes extra) while we stabilize.

I put the two attachment stubs at the bottom: a small CSV snapshot from host metrics and a customer-facing draft to iterate on.

I’m standing by on Zoom — please flag prioritized actions in replies.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv_evap_snapshot.csv (metrics snapshot), bluecart_proactive_note_v1.docx (customer draft)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-06-07T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Interim mitigation plan for service suppression + customer-facing readout

Thanks Steph. Quick findings from runtime:
- Yes, there was a rolling control-plane deploy that started at 08:28 UTC and triggered node restarts for a subset of the GPU pool in us-west-2 that BlueCart is routed to.
- Eviction pattern: KV cache miss ratio jumped from ~4% to ~67% within a 3-minute window, followed by higher GPU kernel setup time (avg kernel init +3.2ms).
- We also observed a short burst of requests that tripped the per-tenant concurrency limiter briefly, which amplified tail latency for streaming calls.

Immediate actions I’ve kicked off (09:30):
1) Paused the rollout across all affected pools (rollback hold).
2) Triggered a one-time routing override to redirect BlueCart to their warm standby pool (should be effective inside 2 minutes).
3) Increased per-tenant concurrency soft-limit for BlueCart by +30% for next 20 minutes to reduce rejects while we stabilize.

Risk notes: routing to a standby pool will add a small cost (higher warm-start headroom), but it should reduce p95 within the 10–15 minute stabilization window.

Next steps for eng: Marcus to validate cache-retention knob; I’ll follow up with logs and a short RCA draft in ~2 hours.

—Ben
Senior SRE
Redwood Inference

--- customer-facing draft (v0.1) ---
Subject: Update on elevated latency this morning (June 7)
Hi Jackie / BlueCart team,

We identified an infrastructure rollout that caused temporary cache eviction and increased latency for a subset of requests routed to your service. Our on-call engineers paused the rollout and routed traffic to warm standby capacity; we expect latency to return to normal within 15–30 minutes and have taken steps to reduce the chance of recurrence.

Immediate actions we took:
- Paused the rollout that triggered node restarts.
- Redirected traffic to already-warmed capacity to restore throughput.
- Raised temporary concurrency limits to reduce request rejects while we stabilize.

What we’re doing next: our engineering team is preparing a short RCA and a plan to add rollout safe-guards that preserve tenant-level caches. We will share that update by EOD today.

If you’d like a call to talk through impact or ask us to coordinate a specific mitigation, let us know and we’ll join immediately.

— Marissa
Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Quick engineering summary for the external RCA + internal tickets:
- Root cause hypothesis: control-plane rollout triggered coordinated node restarts on a fraction of the pool; we do not yet see firmware/kernel faults. The observed KV cache evaporation is consistent with nodes being restarted without a graceful cache-shutdown path.
- Data safety: no evidence of persisted customer data loss — all requests that failed were at the inference-serving layer and were retried upstream by BlueCart; storage systems (S3, DB) show no dropped writes.
- Short-term engineering fixes: add a cache-preserving handshake to the shutdown path and expose a rollout-safe flag that prevents eviction for pinned tenants. I estimate a scoped change + test for the handshake is 2–3 sprints for full productization; a hotfix (patch to reduce eviction window) could be ready in ~5 business days.
- Long-term: we’ll schedule a design ticket to make rollouts cache-safe and add rollout pre-checks for high-throughput tenants.

Ben will drop logs and a short timeline; Marissa — once Jackie confirms the customer copy is ok, send it and we’ll mark the incident as stabilized.

—Marcus
Senior Platform Engineer
Redwood Inference
